prompts.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create one finished horizontal museum art postcard, aspect 3:2, high resolution. Input image is reference only: the authentic Warring States Baoshan painted lacquer box, especially its small processional figures, willow trees, horses, black lacquer ground and vermilion horizontal rules. Make a refined contemporary graphic reinterpretation, NOT a restored artifact photo. Very deep matte lacquer-black background; exquisite thin vermilion-red rules framing the top and bottom and a thin inset outer border. The principal image is five small elegant ancient Chinese side-profile figures in long pale ochre, muted sage and cinnabar robes, flat hand-painted archaic lacquer style, walking/meeting in a horizontal narrative frieze; use the source's stylized proportions and curved silhouettes. Include a slender wind-blown willow tree in each side of the composition, fine red/ochre trunk and sparse delicate leaves. Large disciplined black negative space, confident crisp linework, subtle handmade lacquer grain, no gradients, no modern cartoon, no 3D shading. Upper-right: one empty vermilion-red outlined rectangular postage-stamp-like frame, small and elegant, with a few simple red cancellation arcs; no text, no invented seal letters, no museum logo. The art fills the postcard itself, no desk or mockup scene, no drop shadow. Keep the reference cultural visual language; this is the HUMAN FIGURES edition. No horses or other animals dominating.

Use case: illustration-story. Produce the ANIMALS companion postcard to reference image 1 (the newly designed human postcard), using reference image 2 (authentic Baoshan lacquer box) only as historical visual inspiration. One finished horizontal 3:2 postcard, exact same matte lacquer-black ground, red framing rules, decorative archaic curving bands at top/bottom and small red outlined empty postage stamp with cancellation arcs in upper-right. Replace the people in the main frieze with a lively elongated leaping dog and running wild boar inspired by Warring States lacquer painting, a small poised bird as subordinate motif. Keep graceful wind-blown willow trees on both sides. Flat primitive slender silhouettes, confident vermilion fine linework, sparse warm ochre and muted sage details. Deep black negative space. No people, no chariots, no realistic 3D animals, no modern cartoon, no text, no watermarks. Finished print artwork, fills image edge, not a photo of paper. This is a contemporary motif reinterpretation, not an archaeological restoration. Match companion composition and museum refinement.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Create a VIDEO FIRST FRAME directly based on the authentic figures painted on the Baoshan Warring States lacquer object in the two reference photographs. This is NOT a postcard design. No stamp, no postal mark, no decorative picture frame, no invented border, no graphic design layout, no modern illustration. Reference 1 is the original round lacquer vessel; reference 2 is its painted narrative unfolded into five horizontal strips. Take the human encounter scene and willow from the original: five small archaic side-profile figures with tiny heads, very tall simple curved robe silhouettes and the EXACT primitive profile/headwear language seen on the original. Preserve the original black-green aged lacquer ground, worn earthy red rules, muted yellow, muted sage, warm ochre pigment, abrasions and imperfect ancient brushwork. Do not draw detailed modern faces or elaborate later-dynasty garments. Unroll a close-up of this actual painted narrative into a flat landscape 16:9 frame: five figures in a loose horizontal row across the lower middle, windblown willow branches entering from either edge. The image should feel like magnifying the actual aged painted lacquer wall. Keep the figures proportionally about one-third image height with surrounding dark lacquer breathing room; original thin red painted rules can appear at top and bottom, no ornamental bands. Static starting pose, fixed straight-on camera; quiet and archaeological-looking, no 3D. No text, no labels, no added scene props. This is an animation preparation derived from the original painting; avoid a brand-new imaginative character design.

Use case: precise-object-edit. This provided image is the FIRST FRAME of an animation of figures on the Baoshan lacquer painting itself, not a postcard. Produce the matching FINAL FRAME. Preserve the exact landscape 16:9 canvas, fixed frontal camera, ancient lacquer surface, pigment colors, red horizontal painted rules, worn scratches, trunks and all negative space. Keep exactly the same five archaic figures, identical heads and headgear, simple silhouette forms and garment colors. Make small controlled motion only: the two left figures advance one small step toward the central figure; the central dark-robed figure raises a curved sleeve slightly in greeting; the two right figures incline a little toward the center; willow twig tips shift gently right with a breeze. Movements must remain small (less than 4 percent of frame width), no drastic deformation, keep everyone separated and legible. Preserve the intentionally crude flat ancient painted style: tiny heads, long sweeping robe hems, sparse linework and real worn pigment texture. Do not modernize faces, no decorative postcard frame, no stamp, no postal marks, no extra figures or objects, no writing. This frame will be used as the ending of a 6-second fixed-camera animated painting.
